osps_ac_01_01_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide: GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation, covering repository write access and private vulnerability reports alike.
osps_ac_02_01_justification: Collaborator permissions are assigned explicitly, never inherited by default. The repository baseline script sets the default repository permission to the lowest privilege and review routing goes through CODEOWNERS to the `owners` team; the settings are code, applied and drift-checked by settings/repo-baseline.sh. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
osps_ac_03_01_justification: An organisation-level ruleset blocks direct pushes to main: every change must arrive as a pull request and pass required status checks. The rules and their rationale are recorded in docs/rulesets.md and the Monday audit re-checks them for drift. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The organisation ruleset restricts branch deletion on the primary branch, so deleting main is refused rather than confirmed away. Recorded in docs/rulesets.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_ac_04_01_justification: Least privilege is the default and the explicit setting: the repository baseline sets the workflow token to read-only permissions, and every workflow declares its own minimal `permissions:` block on top of that. A job that specifies nothing therefore gets read, not write. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow declares an explicit `permissions:` block scoped to what that job actually needs, on top of a read-only default set by the repository baseline. The strongest case is enforced by a lint: no workflow that runs caller-supplied code may hold `id-token: write`, and lint:capability-boundary fails the build if one ever does.
osps_br_01_01_justification: Untrusted workflow metadata is validated before use: the shared workflows accept inputs against allowlists (the artifact `classes:` set, the pinned publish stub shape checked by lint:release-stub), and zizmor fails the gate on template-injection patterns where untrusted context would reach a shell.
osps_br_01_03_justification: This is the project's central architectural rule, not an incidental setting: no workflow that runs caller-supplied code may declare `id-token: write`. lint:capability-boundary enforces it in the gate and fails the build if a `workflow_call` workflow ever acquires the privileged identity, so a certificate bearing this repository's identity can never be minted by a job executing a caller's code.
osps_br_01_04_justification: Collaborator-supplied input is validated rather than trusted: workflow inputs are checked against allowlists (the artifact `classes:` set, the release-stub shape), and zizmor fails the gate on any pattern that would interpolate untrusted context into a shell.
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel is HTTPS: the repository, releases, documentation and issue tracker are all served by GitHub over TLS, and no plaintext URI appears in the tree.
osps_br_05_01_justification: Dependency ingestion is standardised: mise with an exact-version config and a lockfile carrying per-platform checksums for tools, and the language-native managers (cargo, npm) for consuming repositories. Preference is for aqua-backed tools so downloads carry checksums and attestations rather than running install scripts.
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning with push protection is enforced by the organisation security configuration, so an unencrypted credential is blocked at push time; trivy's secret rules also run in the gate. The architecture removes most of the risk at source: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, so there are few long-lived secrets to leak.
osps_br_07_02_justification: docs/continuity.md is the secrets policy in operational form: an asset table naming every credential the project uses, where it is stored, who can reach it, and how it is rotated or recreated — including the one standing token, whose expiry is designed to fail loudly rather than silently under-claim. The policy is short because the architecture removes most secrets: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, and no signing key exists to store. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
osps_do_01_01_justification: README.md documents basic usage for consumers (adopt the gate in about six lines, copy scaffold/, run `mise run ci`), and docs/runbook.md is the full operating manual for wiring a repository in and for recovery. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
osps_do_02_01_justification: SUPPORT.md and the repository's issue forms document how to report a defect, and SECURITY.md documents the separate private path for vulnerabilities. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SUPPORT.md
osps_do_03_01_justification: docs/runbook.md has a section written from the consumer's position — 'Verifying as a consumer would' — giving the commands to check a release's attestations and Sigstore evidence bundle against the published digests. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
osps_do_03_02_justification: The same documentation covers authorship identity, which in a keyless design is the workflow identity: verification checks the signer's workflow ref in the certificate rather than a personal key, and the release tooling exposes an explicit signer-workflow flag so a consumer can assert which identity must have signed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
osps_do_04_01_justification: SECURITY.md section 'Supported versions and end of life' states the scope and duration of support: only the latest release of each project receives security updates, fixes ship by rolling forward from main rather than by backporting, and a release is therefore supported exactly until the next release exists. There are no long-term support branches and no announced support windows. A repository with different needs states its own policy in its own SECURITY.md, which then replaces this one for that repository. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_05_01_justification: The same section states when a release stops receiving security updates: a release is end-of-life for security purposes at the point the next release exists, since fixes ship only by rolling forward from main. This is a deliberate consequence of the release design - every release stays reproducible and its evidence permanent, but maintenance effort goes to the tip. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_06_01_justification: Documented in two places and deliberately so: docs/tooling-verdicts.md records how a dependency is selected — the priors a tool must meet to enter the belt, and the verdicts on tools considered and declined — and docs/dependency-track.md records how dependencies are obtained, pinned, monitored and triaged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/tooling-verdicts.md
osps_do_07_01_justification: README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md give the whole sequence: `mise trust && mise install` brings every required tool at its pinned version from the lockfile, and `mise run ci` then runs exactly what CI runs. There are no separate libraries, frameworks or SDKs to install. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_01_01_justification: docs/continuity.md carries an asset table naming who holds each sensitive resource — organisation ownership, the tag-mint App key, registry accounts, the one standing token — and what happens to each if that person is unavailable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
osps_gv_01_02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming three roles - maintainer/owner, contributor, automation - and the responsibilities of each, and it is served from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file so it applies to every repository that does not carry its own. Who holds the maintainer role is explicit: the @monumental-archive/owners team, which CODEOWNERS routes every review to. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
osps_gv_02_01_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests are open for public discussion of proposed changes and usage obstacles; both are searchable and individually addressable by URL. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: open an issue first for anything large, pull requests for small self-contained fixes, Conventional Commits, DCO sign-off, a green `mise run ci`, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md includes a 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: pull request only, a green `mise run ci`, Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects under 72 columns, DCO sign-off, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_04_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md section 'Escalation and permissions' carries the policy: a collaborator is reviewed before being granted any escalated permission. Concretely, before an account joins @monumental-archive/owners or receives write access anywhere, the maintainer reviews who they are, why the access is needed and what the smallest sufficient grant is - and the grant is then recorded in the settings-as-code baseline so drift is auditable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#escalation-and-permissions
osps_le_01_01_justification: Every commit must carry a Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1 sign-off asserting legal authorisation. The commit-msg hook catches a missing trailer locally and lint:dco fails the gate, with no exemption list — automation signs off too.
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released assets carry the same 0BSD licence as the source; there is no separate licence for releases. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_01_justification: LICENSE at the repository root and the full text in LICENSES/0BSD.txt, the REUSE-standard location. api.reuse.software independently reports the project compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: Released assets ship from this repository, which carries LICENSE at its root and LICENSES/0BSD.txt alongside, with per-file attribution recorded in REUSE.toml. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_01_justification: Publicly readable at a static URL. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git records what changed, who changed it and when, for every revision, and the history is public. Beyond that, each revision carries a signed source-provenance attestation, so the record is independently verifiable rather than merely readable.
osps_qa_02_01_justification: mise/config.toml lists every direct tool dependency at an exact version, and mise.lock records per-platform checksums for each. Renovate reads the same file natively. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/mise/config.toml
osps_qa_03_01_justification: The gate is a required status check on main under an organisation ruleset: a pull request cannot merge red, and direct pushes are blocked entirely, so no commit reaches the primary branch without its checks passing. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The organisation's repositories and their status are documented rather than assumed: docs/migration-playbook.md records which codebases join the governance and how, and the scheduled audit enumerates the live repository population from the GitHub API rather than from a hand-kept list. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/migration-playbook.md
osps_qa_04_02_justification: A release of this project comprises this single source repository; there are no subprojects releasing alongside it. Other repositories in the organisation consume this one's governance, which is by construction as strict or stricter.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executable artifacts are committed. The repository contains shell tasks, workflow YAML, configuration and documentation; tools arrive at runtime through mise from pinned, checksummed downloads rather than being vendored.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: No unreviewable binary artifacts are committed — every tracked file is text and reviewable in a diff.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: gate.yml runs the full automated suite — `mise run ci`, every belt check against every tracked file — on each pull request before it can be accepted, and it does so by self-applying the reusable workflow this project publishes. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
osps_qa_06_02_justification: Documented in both places a reader would look: README.md states that `mise run ci` locally is exactly what CI runs, and CONTRIBUTING.md makes a green gate a requirement for every change. When they run is equally explicit — on every pull request and every push to main, with the network-bound checks on a Monday schedule. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_06_03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, item 3 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions', is the policy and it sits in the contributor-facing documentation: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it - a test that fails without the change where a test suite exists, or a lint, audit task or workflow assertion where the product is configuration and policy - and a bug fix adds the case that reproduced the bug. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_07_01_justification: With a single maintainer there is no non-author human approval available, so this is not enforced. It is the headcount wall this project records rather than works around: the same boundary as Gold's two_person_review and SLSA Source L4, tracked as an open issue rather than quietly claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
osps_sa_01_01_justification: docs/release.md specifies the pipeline actor by actor and action by action — what each workflow does, which identity it runs as, what it is permitted to touch — and docs/build-track.md and docs/source-track.md carry the per-track designs. The capability boundary between caller code and the privileged identity is stated explicitly as a design rule. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/release.md
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The external interfaces are the reusable workflows and the task contract: docs/runbook.md documents each workflow's inputs and the artifact classes with their required parameters, and workflow-templates/ ships a caller stub per workflow. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
osps_sa_03_01_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md are written security assessments of this system: they walk the controls, name the most likely and impactful failure modes (untrusted caller code reaching a privileged signing identity, supply-chain substitution through unpinned dependencies, silent settings drift), and record which are mitigated and which are accepted. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
osps_sa_03_02_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md carry the threat model and attack-surface analysis: the critical paths are named (caller code reaching a privileged signing identity, unpinned supply-chain substitution, silent settings drift, forged signer identities in the transparency log), each with the control that protects it and the residual risk accepted. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md is the coordinated disclosure policy and it states the timeframe: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, and what the reporter can expect afterwards. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contact and the reporting channel: private vulnerability reporting through the repository's Security tab, with a 14-day acknowledgement commitment. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_03_01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, delivering the report directly to the security contact without public exposure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerability data is published rather than held privately: resolved reports would be published as GitHub Security Advisories on the repository, and the dependency track already publishes machine-readable VEX decisions keyed by package and version for the advisories that touch this project's dependencies. No vulnerability in this project's own code has been discovered to date. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_04_02_justification: Exactly this: the dependency track emits VEX documents keyed by package@version recording non-exploitability decisions for advisories that do not affect the project, with coverage derived rather than asserted, and the release path refuses to publish while an advisory in the SBOM is undecided. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_05_01_justification: docs/dependency-track.md defines the thresholds: cargo-deny bans and licence rules are deterministic and fail the gate, sources are restricted to a single registry with unknown-registry and unknown-git denied, and every advisory must exit through an explicit decision rather than being left open. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_05_02_justification: The policy is enforced at the release boundary, not merely stated: the release path refuses to publish with an undecided advisory in its SBOM. It has already blocked a real release in the lab rather than being theoretical. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_05_03_justification: Automatically, on every change: cargo-deny runs deterministically in the gate over the lockfile and the committed deny.toml, dependency-review runs on every pull request, and Renovate and Dependabot raise updates as advisories land. The policy those checks enforce is written in docs/dependency-track.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_06_01_justification: SECURITY.md section 'Static analysis policy' defines the remediation threshold, and it is zero: any SAST finding - CodeQL, the lint belt, zizmor and peers - fails the CI gate, and a red gate cannot merge, so findings are remediated or explicitly and reviewably suppressed with a written reason before the change lands. There is no severity triage queue for static findings because there is no state in which one is outstanding on a default branch. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_06_02_justification: Every change is automatically evaluated and blocked on violation: CodeQL default setup is enforced organisation-wide, and shellcheck, actionlint, zizmor and trivy run in the gate, which is a required status check that a pull request cannot merge past. The requirement that the gate pass is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md; what is missing is only a stated severity threshold, recorded honestly under osps_vm_06_01. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
access_continuity_justification: docs/continuity.md is exactly this document: assets and their recovery paths, a break-glass procedure for the tag-minting App, a succession plan, and an explicit list of deliberate single points of failure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The project has no bespoke website: documentation is plain Markdown rendered by GitHub, which is keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly, and the content is text with descriptive link text rather than images carrying meaning.
assurance_case_justification: docs/release.md and docs/slsa-reference.md are the written assurance case, and docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md assess each claim against its evidence: the threat model (untrusted caller code reaching a privileged identity, unpinned supply-chain substitution, tampered artifacts), the countermeasures (the capability boundary, SHA pinning with checksums and attestations, keyless signing with transparency-log evidence), and an explicit record of what is NOT claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
build_floss_tools_justification: No build step exists (see the build criterion).
build_preserve_debug_justification: No build or installation system exists.
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1 — a single maintainer. Recorded plainly in docs/slsa-reference.md as headcount-blocked, with docs/continuity.md carrying the succession and break-glass paths that exist precisely because of it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
code_of_conduct_justification: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md at the repository root, in the standard location, and served as the organisation default to every repository in the org. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: GOVERNANCE.md section 'Code review' documents how review is conducted and what must be checked: that the change does what it says, that the claim it makes is one its checks actually enforce, that it does not weaken a documented control, and that documentation changed alongside behaviour - with the mechanical floor (formatting, linting, licence headers, commit shape, tests) left to the CI gate rather than the reviewer. What is required to be acceptable is stated too: a green gate, resolved review threads enforced by ruleset, a DCO sign-off on every commit, and a PR title and body fit to become the permanent squash commit. It also records that with one maintainer there is no second human reviewer, and names the gate as the compensating control. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Automatically, in the gate: shellcheck, actionlint, zizmor, rumdl, typos and committed all run in `mise run ci` on every pull request, and `fix:*` siblings apply the machine-fixable subset. Style is never a review comment here.
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md names the gate as the coding standard in executable form, and the standards are specific per language: shellcheck for shell (with bash pinned by `[task_config] shell` because Ubuntu's sh is dash), actionlint and zizmor for workflow YAML, rumdl for Markdown, typos for spelling with the locale registers written down, and Conventional Commits with a 72-column subject ceiling. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the process explicitly: fork/branch, conventional imperative commit subjects under 72 columns enforced by committed, DCO sign-off, `mise run ci` green locally, pull request, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: every change arrives by pull request, must pass `mise run ci` (the coding standard in executable form), uses Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects, and is squash-merged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: There is one significant contributor, so there cannot be two unassociated ones. Headcount, not policy: contributions are welcomed under CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
copyright_per_file_justification: Every file carries a copyright statement, attached through REUSE.toml rather than as an inline comment in each file — the REUSE specification's supported mechanism for files that cannot carry headers. `reuse lint` reports 141 of 141 files with copyright information, and lint:reuse enforces it in the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/REUSE.toml
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The project implements no cryptography and selects no algorithms; where cryptography is used it is Sigstore's and GitHub's, whose algorithm choices the project does not control.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptographic operations are delegated to software built for the purpose — Sigstore/cosign, GitHub's attestation tooling and git — never reimplemented here.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The software stores no authentication credentials or private keys at all. Secrets live in GitHub environment and organisation secrets, never in files in the repository, and release signing uses ephemeral keys.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptography relied on is implementable with FLOSS: Sigstore, cosign and git are open source.
crypto_keylength_justification: The project selects no keylengths. Release signing uses ephemeral Sigstore keys with Fulcio-issued certificates, and transport keys belong to GitHub.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The software stores no passwords and authenticates no external users.
crypto_pfs_justification: The software implements no key agreement protocol; it is configuration and workflows, not a network service.
crypto_published_justification: The project implements no cryptography of its own. Where it relies on cryptography it uses published, expert-reviewed mechanisms: Sigstore (Fulcio certificates, Rekor transparency log), GitHub artifact attestations, SHA-256 checksums and OpenPGP-free keyless signing.
crypto_random_justification: The software generates no cryptographic keys or nonces; release signing keys are generated by Sigstore.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Integrity everywhere is SHA-256 — per-platform checksums in mise.lock, image digests, attestation subjects — and signing is Sigstore's ECDSA P-256. No MD5 or SHA-1 is relied on as a security mechanism.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm is depended on for security: artifact integrity uses SHA-256 (per-platform checksums in mise.lock, image digests, attestation subjects) and signing uses Sigstore's ECDSA P-256.
dco_justification: Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1. Every commit must carry Signed-off-by; the commit-msg hook catches it locally and lint:dco enforces it in the gate, with no exemption list — the release commit and Renovate sign off too. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
delivery_mitm_justification: Everything is delivered over HTTPS by GitHub. Beyond transport, the toolbelt pins every tool by exact version with per-platform checksums in mise.lock and verifies GitHub attestations, and every uses: is pinned to a full commit SHA.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Checksums are not fetched over http at use time: they are committed in mise.lock in this repository and travel with the source, and releases additionally carry Sigstore evidence bundles.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests: searchable, individually addressable by URL, open to new participants, and archived publicly. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/issues
documentation_roadmap_justification: docs/direction.md is the roadmap and it is unusually explicit about what the project will NOT do: a target table naming the level intended on each SLSA track, the claims policy, and the ceilings and why each sits where it does (BuildEnv is L0 by attribution, not by choice: its controls are built, but the signed build-image provenance that would make them a level belongs to producers who do not emit it; Gold-level criteria are not claimed while there is one maintainer). Open items are tracked as issues and the table is the first thing a closing issue updates. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/direction.md
english_justification: All documentation, code comments, issues and commit messages are in English (en-US in code and identifiers, en-GB in prose, a convention recorded in CLAUDE.md).
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are filed as issues, triaged, and either scheduled with a linked pull request or closed with the reason recorded; none are left unanswered.
floss_license_justification: Released under 0BSD, a FLOSS licence. LICENSE at the repository root, full text in LICENSES/0BSD.txt, per-file attribution via REUSE.toml, enforced in the gate by lint:licence and lint:reuse. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/LICENSE
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents the decision model explicitly rather than aspirationally: one maintainer deciding in the open, significant decisions made in writing and in public before they are implemented (the docs-first standup, recorded as issues and pull requests), declined paths recorded with reasons so they are re-litigated against the record, and a written succession plan. It is served from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file, so it governs every repository that does not carry its own. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
input_validation_justification: The shared workflows validate their inputs against allowlists rather than trusting callers: the artifact `classes:` input accepts only a known set, the publish stub's filename and shape are checked by lint:release-stub, and workflow inputs that would otherwise be interpolated into shell are guarded — zizmor fails the gate on template-injection patterns.
interact_justification: The README links CONTRIBUTING.md (how to contribute), SUPPORT.md (how to get help) and SECURITY.md (how to report vulnerabilities); issue forms and a pull-request template are provided in .github/. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github
internationalization_justification: The software produced is shell tasks, workflows and configuration; it emits maintainer-facing diagnostics only and has no end-user interface strings to localise.
know_common_errors_justification: The documented threat reasoning covers the error classes specific to this software: credential exfiltration through untrusted workflow input (enforced by zizmor and the capability-boundary lint), unpinned actions and supply-chain substitution (every uses: pinned to a full commit SHA with checksums and attestations), and secret exposure in logs. See docs/slsa-reference.md and docs/build-assessment.md.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer designed and documented the project's security architecture: least privilege in workflows, an explicit capability boundary forbidding id-token: write in any workflow that runs caller-supplied code, keyless trusted publishing instead of long-lived tokens, and SLSA Build/Source/Dependency track conformance with written assurance in docs/slsa-reference.md and docs/release.md.
license_location_justification: LICENSE at the repository root and LICENSES/0BSD.txt in the REUSE-standard location; api.reuse.software reports the project REUSE-compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/LICENSE
license_per_file_justification: Every file carries an SPDX licence statement (0BSD) through REUSE.toml, with the full text in LICENSES/0BSD.txt. `reuse lint` reports 141 of 141 files with licence information and api.reuse.software independently reports the project compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/REUSE.toml
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: releases are cut continuously from conventional commits, Renovate and Dependabot keep pins current, and a scheduled Monday audit re-checks settings drift, link liveness and badge truth.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Consumers pin this repository by tag or commit SHA and move at their own pace; MAINTENANCE.md documents the versioned surface, what a release means and what may change between versions, and Renovate opens the upgrade pull request for every consumer automatically. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/MAINTENANCE.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credential is committed. GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enforced by the organisation security configuration, trivy's secret rules run in the gate, and the design avoids long-lived credentials entirely: publishing is keyless via trusted publishing and OIDC.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands as a pull request with its own commits; the repository contains the full development history, not only released states.
repo_track_justification: Git records author, committer, timestamp and diff for every change; history is protected by org rulesets and every revision carries a signed source-provenance attestation (SLSA Source L3).
report_archive_justification: The issue tracker is public and permanently archived and searchable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_process_justification: Bug reports are submitted through GitHub Issues using the repository's issue forms; SUPPORT.md states where to ask. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/issues/new/choose
report_responses_justification: Every issue filed in the last 12 months has been acknowledged and triaged by the maintainer; the tracker carries no unanswered reports.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues, used for every individual issue. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/issues
require_2FA_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide — GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation — so it covers pushing to the repository and access to private vulnerability reports alike.
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming three roles - maintainer/owner, contributor, automation - and what each is responsible for. Who holds the maintainer role is unambiguous: the @monumental-archive/owners team, which CODEOWNERS routes every review to in every repository, and joining that team is what becoming a maintainer concretely means. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
secure_2FA_justification: The 2FA in use is cryptographic rather than SMS-based: GitHub's supported second factors here are TOTP and WebAuthn, and the organisation's requirement is satisfied without SMS.
security_review_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md are security reviews written against this project's own security requirements and boundary, control by control, and docs/slsa-reference.md records what is claimed and what is deliberately not. They are current, not historical: the scheduled audit re-checks the claims they rest on. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
sites_https_justification: The repository, its releases and its documentation are served by GitHub over HTTPS; there is no separate project website.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub; the project stores no passwords of its own.
small_tasks_justification: Open issues are labelled 'good first issue' and 'help wanted': #4 (absorb the renovate-config repository and retire it) and #27 (stand up GitHub Sponsors and a FUNDING.yml). Both are self-contained and can be completed without prior context in the release machinery. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/labels/good%20first%20issue
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: zizmor is a vulnerability scanner specific to what this project produces — GitHub Actions workflows — covering template injection, excessive permissions, credential persistence and unpinned actions. CodeQL default setup is enforced organisation-wide and trivy adds misconfiguration and secret rules. All run in the gate on every pull request.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings are fixed before merge — the gate blocks the pull request, so no finding of medium or higher severity has ever reached main unaddressed.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL default setup is enforced organisation-wide, and the gate additionally runs shellcheck over every tracked shell task, actionlint and zizmor over every workflow, and trivy over configuration — on every pull request, before any release.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every commit: the gate runs on every pull request and every push to main, and a scheduled Monday audit re-runs the network-dependent checks.
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' item 3, is the formal written policy: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it - a test that fails without the change where a test suite exists, and a lint, audit task or workflow assertion in configuration and policy repositories. It is stated as policy: the gate's checks are the specification, and functionality nothing enforces is functionality the next change may silently remove. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added_justification: The most recent major changes each shipped their own gate task: lint:badges with the derived badge block, lint:licence with the licence policy, lint:citation with the derived CITATION.cff, and lint:capability-boundary with the id-token boundary rule.
tests_documented_added_justification: The policy is stated in the documented instructions for change proposals themselves: CONTRIBUTING.md, item 3 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' - a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it, and a bug fix adds the case that reproduced the bug. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
two_person_review_justification: With a single maintainer, no proposed modification is reviewed by a person other than its author. This is the Source L4 and Gold boundary for this project and is recorded as headcount-blocked in docs/slsa-reference.md; it is watched as an issue rather than papered over. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Critical vulnerabilities are fixed as soon as they are identified; dependency updates are automated and the release gate blocks on the dependency checks.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities of medium or higher severity. Renovate and Dependabot open updates continuously, trivy runs in the gate, and the dependency track records VEX decisions keyed by package and version.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability report has been resolved in the last 12 months, so there is no reporter to credit. SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters who do not request anonymity.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, so reports stay private until an advisory is published. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md publishes the process: private reporting through the repository's Security tab. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received in the last 6 months, so there is no response time to report. SECURITY.md commits to acknowledgement within 14 days.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents the process end to end: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, what to expect afterwards, and the scope. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
